title: Accessible anywhere: Pfizer uses AVEVA PI System for production analysis
summary: Pfizer models each production room and its equipment in AF and publishes the data to AWS for analysis in Spotfire. A PI Vision floor-plan dashboard and a second PI server set for utilities and building management complete the picture.
challenge: Data was siloed, staff exported CSV files to Excel by hand, and 8 to 12 utility and building automation systems had mismatched timestamps.
solution: AF equipment and process models; analyses that compute yield and capture event frame snapshots at the start and end of each batch; GMP, non-GMP, GLP and GCP data held on local servers.

outcomes.text: Subject-matter experts save five to 10 hours per week

title: GlaxoSmithKline improves sustainability with AVEVA PI System
summary: GSK uses PI System together with AVEVA System Platform and AVEVA Reports as the foundation of its "Factory of the Future".
challenge: GSK wanted more efficiency, more standardisation and faster technology transfer.
solution: An integrated platform for operational information built on PI System and System Platform.

title: AVEVA PI System is at the heart of Dr. Reddy's Laboratories' digital transformation
summary: Dr. Reddy's uses PI System for real-time streaming analytics that monitor processes against specification limits, as the core of its digital transformation.
challenge: Equipment efficiency, downtime, batch failures and paper-based outputs were all problems.
solution: PI System as the core of the digital transformation programme.

outcomes.text: "40% reduction in quality-related costs" at its flagship site

title: Migrating a pharmaceutical facility to event frames
summary: Genentech, with Control Systems Integration, migrated 7.2 million batch events (dating from April 2006) from PI Batch to Event Frames in a validated system.
challenge: KPIs were kept in spreadsheets, and not all data was linked to PI Batch.
solution: A virtual development environment, event frame templates built from user requirements, and the EMDVB interface on PI Server 2015 R2 / AF Server 2015 R2.

outcomes.text: User-reported time savings and data confidence (no figures given)
outcomes.reportedBy: Genentech and Control Systems Integration in an OSIsoft UC 2016 presentation

outcomes.text: 3 days of downtime affecting batch data only
outcomes.reportedBy: Genentech and Control Systems Integration in an OSIsoft UC 2016 presentation

title: Migrated and validated billions of data points to AVEVA PI System
summary: Genentech and RoviSys migrated about 20 years of data from a legacy historian into PI System with zero downtime, proving the move kept 100% data integrity.
challenge: No downtime was allowed, and the team had to prove data integrity.
solution: Migration and validation carried out with RoviSys.

outcomes.text: "Moved 130 billion events across 27,000 AVEVA PI System tags"

title: Combining laboratory and process data on the PI System
summary: Janssen Cork modelled AF on S88, linking lab-measured critical quality attributes (CQAs) to critical process parameters (CPPs) to support continued process verification (CPV).
challenge: Lab and process data sat in separate systems.
solution: One AF element per process, a sub-element per CQA and child elements for CPPs mapped to PI tags; PI ACE writes to SQL, and lab results come from ELIMS.

outcomes.text: Qualitative: CPV extended to a broad user base (no figures given)
outcomes.reportedBy: The company (Kevin Crean) in an OSIsoft UC 2013 presentation

title: GxP compliant alarm handling with event frames and AF
summary: Roche and OctaveSoft built RIPIN (Roche Interface for PI Event Frames), a GxP-compliant alarm interface that replaced OSIsoft's PI AlarmView.
challenge: Roche had to replace the legacy PI AlarmView in a GxP context.
solution: Standard event frame templates, AF as a meta database, and web-based alarm acknowledgement and annotation.

outcomes.reportedBy: Roche and OctaveSoft in an OSIsoft UC 2016 abstract

title: Bringing Alzheimer's drug within reach with AVEVA PI System
summary: Biogen uses contextualised PI data on the plant floor for real-time review by exception before batches advance.
challenge: No real-time visibility in a strictly regulated process.
solution: Contextualised PI data available on the plant floor.

outcomes.text: No measured figures. Goals only: reduce costs "from $10,000 to $100-150 per gram" and make enough drug for one million patients.

verifyNote: The cost figures are goals, not measured results.

title: Empowering operators with real-time fault detection
summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb built real-time multivariate monitoring with AF so operators can detect faults during batches.
challenge: Batch data arrived late and lacked context.
solution: Monitoring "built with out-of-the-box tools in the asset framework".

outcomes.reportedBy: AVEVA (customer success story); the same team presented at PI World 2019

title: Biotech scale-up uses FTView and AVEVA PI Historian
summary: An unnamed biotech, working with integrator E Tech Group, scaled up to cGMP manufacturing with the audit trail enabled on PI Server and a full validation lifecycle.
challenge: Islands of automation, some of which predated 21 CFR Part 11.
solution: URS, FS and SDS documents, FAT and SAT testing, and access limited to authorised users through Active Directory.
